# Ink

> A design library with a printed edge and a glass bar. Framework-agnostic tokens
> and behaviour, React and React Native bindings, and plain CSS for everything
> else. Zero runtime dependencies.

Ink separates what a component *decides* from what it *looks like*. Tokens,
geometry, WCAG maths and behaviour state machines have no framework in them and
run anywhere; the React and React Native packages are thin renderers over that
shared core, and the stylesheet drives any framework with no JavaScript at all.

Two things distinguish it: the **ink edge** is modelled as a static plate behind
a moving face rather than an animated shadow, which is what makes it drawable on
React Native; and every contrast-sensitive colour is **derived from a measured
floor** rather than chosen, including the glass tint, so a runtime-selected
accent cannot produce an unreadable control.

## Docs

- [Agent reference](docs/AGENTS.md): complete API, rules and import paths, written for coding agents
- [README](README.md): human-facing overview and getting started
- [Inventory](docs/INVENTORY.md): every element, and what is deliberately absent
- [Glass](docs/GLASS.md): the derived-tint material and the navbar's behaviour

## Entry points

- `@jarida/ink` — tokens, geometry, contrast, headless behaviour. No dependencies.
- `@jarida/ink/headless` — navbar / roving focus / toast / slider state machines
- `@jarida/ink/css` — the stylesheet, usable from any framework
- `@jarida/ink/react` — React DOM components
- `@jarida/ink/native` — React Native / Expo components
